readout_other: Somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) via epidural cortical grid electrode following trigeminal, median, and tibial nerve stimulation; MR thermometry (proton-resonance-frequency shift); H&E and Luxol Fast Blue histology
direction_notes: LIFU sonication of the VPL/VPM decreased (suppressed) somatosensory/trigeminal evoked potentials in a target-specific manner, with recovery to near-baseline within ~10-20 minutes; off-target and contralateral control sonications had no significant effect.
safety_notes: No observable temperature increases at the acoustic focus during LIFU sonications (sensitivity <1 degrees C), and no gross or microscopic histological evidence of tissue damage in LIFU-treated thalamus.

exposures.label: LIFU of right ventroposterolateral thalamic nucleus (VPL)

device.manufacturer: FUS Instruments, Inc. (1.14 MHz); InSightec (650/220 kHz)
device.model: RK-100 (1.14 MHz); ExAblate Neuro (650 kHz and 220 kHz phased arrays)

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound experiments at 1.14 MHz used a preclinical single-element FUS system; experiments at 650(710) kHz and 220 kHz used the clinical ExAblate Neuro (InSightec) phased-array systems, with the same duty cycle and sonication duration maintained across all three systems. Off-target control sonications (2 mm anterior to VPM) and contralateral control sonications (left VPL) were also performed as anatomical specificity controls. HIFU sonications (continuous-wave, 20 W, 20 s) were used separately to verify targeting/thermometry and to create ablative lesions for comparison, not as a neuromodulation exposure.

flags.reason: N=10 is stated for the combined histology cohort (8 LIFU + 6 HIFU, overlapping); different sub-experiments (e.g., N=4 animals for thalamic mapping) report different subject counts, and no single 'total subjects in study' sentence is given.

Paper is internally inconsistent about the clinical transducer frequency: the Methods section header says 'Clinical 710 and 220 kHz FUS systems' while the same paragraph and Figure 1 caption say '650 kHz'; both target VPL and VPM are reported to have been tested across all three transducers with the same intensity/duty-cycle protocol, but outcome percentages in Fig. 3 are not broken down by frequency.

Different devices (custom 1.14 MHz single-element system vs. clinical InSightec ExAblate Neuro at 650/220 kHz) were used across the frequency list within this single exposure entry; a single device object cannot fully represent this.
Paper reports this value as 'ISA' (spatial-average intensity), not explicitly Isppa or Ispta, and does not state whether it is a free-field or in-situ value.
